lessons.name: Component API Design
lessons.desc: Props interface, naming conventions, required vs optional, TypeScript generics for component APIs
terms: component ke wo saare props jo bahar wale use karte hain
ek prop jo user ko default behaviour se bahar nikalne deta hai (className, render)
har nayi zaroorat pe naya prop — 20 props ka component
lessons.what:
Definition: Component API design ka matlab hai — component ka public contract tay karna: kaunse props, kya naam, kya required, kya default, aur kya nahi dena.

Design round mein interviewer sabse pehle yahi poochta hai — "iska API kya hoga?" Tumhara jawab props ki list nahi, ek soch honi chahiye: kaunsa data zaroori hai, kaunsa optional, aur user ko kahan control chahiye.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant ka menu. Chhota menu = har dish achhi banti hai. 200 item ka menu = kitchen confuse, quality kharab. Component bhi wahi — chhota, saaf API zyada bharosemand hota hai.
lessons.why:
Ek baar API public ho gaya to usko badalna breaking change hai. Design system mein ek prop rename karne ka matlab 200 files ka refactor. Isliye interview mein log dekhte hain ki tum aage sochte ho ya nahi.

Sabse aam galti: har nayi requirement pe naya boolean prop — isBig, isRed, hasIcon, showBorder. 6 mahine baad 22 props aur koi combination samajh nahi aata. Iska ilaaj hai variant + composition.

"iska API kya hoga" ka jawab yahin se aata hai
pros: Union variant se impossible combination ban hi nahi sakta
...rest se native props free mein pass through
Chhota API = kam breaking changes, kam docs
cons: Variant approach mein "sirf ek chhota sa farak" wale case mushkil
Escape hatch (className) dene se design system ki consistency toot sakti hai
Composition seekhne mein waqt lagta hai — props zyada obvious lagte hain
gotchas: Design round mein API pehle bolo, implementation baad mein — interviewer isi ka intezaar kar raha hota hai
...rest spread ko apne props ke BAAD rakho (ya pehle) — soch samajh ke decide karo kaun jeete
Boolean prop tabhi jab wo sach mein binary ho — teen state ho to string union lo

lessons.name: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
lessons.desc: When each fits, forwardRef, useImperativeHandle, ref forwarding patterns
terms: value parent ke state se aati hai
component apni value khud rakhta hai
dono support karna — value diya to controlled, nahi to internal
lessons.what:
Definition: Design round mein sirf "controlled vs uncontrolled" batana kaafi nahi — dono support karo. Production component ka standard yahi hai: value prop diya to controlled, nahi diya to component apna state rakh le (defaultValue se shuru).

Ye pattern har achhi library mein hai — Radix, MUI, React Aria sab.
lessons.analogy: Car ka cruise control. Tum chaho to khud accelerator dabao (controlled), chaho to gaadi khud speed rakhe (uncontrolled). Dono option honi chahiye — sirf ek dena ziddi design hai.
lessons.why:
90% use cases mein user ko value ki parwah nahi hoti — usse bas ek working dropdown chahiye. Un 90% ko controlled banane pe majboor karna matlab har jagah bekaar ka useState. Par baaki 10% (form library ke saath, ya value ko URL se sync karna) ko control chahiye hi chahiye.

Hybrid pattern dono ko khush karta hai — aur ek useControllableState hook likh ke poore design system mein reuse ho jaata hai.
where: RHF ko controlled chahiye hota hai
pros: Simple case simple rehta hai, complex case possible
Ek hook poore design system mein reuse
onChange dono modes mein fire hota hai — analytics/validation kaam karta hai
cons: Thoda extra code har component mein
Mode beech mein switch ho jaaye to bugs
Interviewer ko dono branches ka reasoning batana padta hai
gotchas: undefined se value aa jaana = uncontrolled se controlled switch — dev warning zaroor daalo
onChange uncontrolled mode mein bhi call hona chahiye, warna consumer andha ho jaayega
Controlled mode mein internal state ko update MAT karo — warna do source of truth

lessons.name: Compound Components Pattern
lessons.desc: Implicit state sharing via Context, flexible composition, dot notation API (Tabs.Panel etc.)
terms: kai components jo milkar ek widget banate hain
parent ka state jo children ko Context se apne aap milta hai
wo jagah jahan user apna content daal sakta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Ek parent state rakhta hai aur Context se apne bacchon ko deta hai. User HTML jaisa likhta hai — <Tabs><Tabs.List><Tabs.Tab/></Tabs.List><Tabs.Panel/></Tabs>.

Design round mein ye flexibility ka jawab hai — jab interviewer poochta hai "agar client tab ke beech ek divider chahe to?"
lessons.why:
Config-object API (<Tabs items={[...]} />) tab tak theek hai jab tak layout fixed ho. Pehli custom requirement aate hi — "tab ke saath badge", "divider", "tabs neeche" — tumhe naya prop add karna padta hai. Compound mein layout user ka hai, tumhara sirf behaviour (state, keyboard, ARIA).

Yahi wajah hai ki Radix/Headless UI sab compound hain — wo behaviour dete hain, look nahi.

Prop explosion khatam
Behaviour (keyboard, ARIA) ek jagah — har consumer ko free mein
cons: Implicit dependency — galat jagah use karne pe runtime error
Zyada boilerplate chhote widgets ke liye
TypeScript mein dot-notation ke types thode extra kaam maangte hain
gotchas: Context null check karke saaf error throw karo — "cannot read of null" se bahut behtar
React.Children.map se children inspect mat karo — nested wrapper aate hi toot jaata hai
Context value useMemo karo warna har render pe saare tabs re-render

lessons.name: Composition over Configuration
lessons.desc: children pattern, render props, slot pattern — avoiding prop explosion
terms: ek component ko props se sab kuch batana
named prop jisme JSX aata hai — header, footer, actions
lessons.what:
Definition: Do rasta hai flexibility dene ka:

  • Configuration — <Card title icon actions showBorder />. Simple, par har naya case naya prop.
  • Composition — <Card><Card.Header/><Card.Body/></Card>. Zyada likhna, par unlimited flexibility.

Beech ka rasta: slots — <Card header={<X/>} footer={<Y/>} />.
lessons.why:
Rule of thumb jo interview mein bolne layak hai: "Config for data, composition for structure." Jo cheez data hai (title text, disabled) wo prop rahe. Jo cheez structure hai (kya kahan dikhega) wo children/slot se aaye.

Bonus jo log bhool jaate hain: composition ka ek performance fayda bhi hai — children parent ke bahar bante hain, isliye parent ka state badalne pe unka element reference wahi rehta hai aur React unka render skip kar deta hai.
where: wrapper ke state ko heavy child se alag karna
pros: Nayi requirement pe naya prop nahi lagta
Composition ka free performance benefit
Component ka code chhota rehta hai
cons: Call site verbose ho jaata hai
Structure enforce nahi hota — user kuch bhi daal sakta hai
Simple cases over-engineered lag sakte hain
gotchas: Interview mein "config for data, composition for structure" bolna — ye rule sabko impress karta hai
Slots (ReactNode props) beech ka rasta hai — structure fix chahiye par content flexible
Children as props ka perf benefit zaroor mention karo — bahut kam log ye jaante hain

lessons.name: State Colocation
lessons.desc: Keep state as close to usage as possible — lifting vs drilling vs context vs global store
terms: state ko usi jagah ke paas rakhna jahan wo use hota hai
state ko common parent tak upar le jaana
props ko 4-5 level neeche pass karte jaana
lessons.what:
Definition: State ko utna hi upar rakho jitna zaroori hai — ek level bhi zyada nahi. Default sabse neeche; jab do bhaiyon ko chahiye tabhi upar uthao.

Design round mein ye performance ka sabse pehla jawab hai — memo se pehle.
lessons.analogy: Ghar ka saamaan. Chai ka cup kitchen mein rakho, store room mein nahi. Jo cheez sirf ek kamre mein use hoti hai, usko common area mein rakhne se sab ko dikkat hoti hai.
lessons.why:
State jitni upar hogi, uska update utna bada subtree re-render karega. Ek modal ka isOpen agar App mein hai to modal kholne pe poora app render hota hai. Wahi state Modal ke paas rakho to sirf wo render hoga.

Interview mein ye batao: "pehle main state ko neeche push karta hoon, memo aakhri raasta hai" — kyunki memo ki apni cost hai, colocation free hai.

Component portable ho jaata hai — kahin bhi utha ke rakh do

Deep tree mein prop drilling badh sakti hai

Do siblings ko chahiye tabhi lift karo — pehle se nahi
Interview mein bolo "pehle colocation, phir composition, aakhir mein memo" — yahi sahi order hai

lessons.name: Accessibility-first Design
lessons.desc: ARIA roles/states/properties, keyboard navigation, focus management, screen reader testing
terms: Accessible Rich Internet Applications — screen reader ke liye extra info
group mein sirf ek element tab-focusable, baaki arrow keys se
modal ke andar focus ko band rakhna
lessons.what:
Definition: Accessibility ko baad mein "add" nahi kiya jaata — component ke design mein hi aata hai. Char cheezein har widget mein chahiye:

  1. Semantic HTML — <button>, <nav>, <dialog> (div pe onClick nahi)
  2. Keyboard — Tab, Enter/Space, Arrow, Escape, Home/End
  3. ARIA — role, state (aria-expanded), relationship (aria-controls)
  4. Focus management — kholne pe kahan jaaye, band karne pe kahan lauth aaye
lessons.why:
Interview mein a11y mention karna seniority ka signal hai — bahut kam log karte hain. Aur practically: <div onClick> keyboard se click nahi hota, screen reader use padhta hi nahi, aur Enter key kaam nahi karti. <button> ye teeno free mein deta hai.

Sabse achha rule: pehle sahi HTML element chuno. Aadhi a11y wahin ho jaati hai. ARIA tab lagao jab HTML mein wo cheez hai hi nahi (tabs, combobox).

Keyboard users, screen reader users, power users sabko fayda

cons: Testing ke liye actual screen reader chahiye (NVDA/VoiceOver)
ARIA galat lagana ARIA na lagane se bura hai
Focus management mein bahut edge cases
gotchas: ARIA ka pehla rule: koi ARIA nahi > galat ARIA. Sahi HTML element pehle chuno.
aria-label se native text override ho jaata hai — screen reader wahi padhega, visible text nahi
Focus outline kabhi mat hatao — :focus-visible se style karo, display mat karo none

lessons.name: Virtualization / Windowing
lessons.desc: Only render visible rows — react-window, TanStack Virtual, overscan, dynamic row heights
terms: sirf visible items ka DOM banana
window ke thoda bahar extra rows — scroll smooth rakhne ko
har row ki alag height — sabse mushkil case
lessons.what:
Definition: 10,000 rows ka DOM browser ko maar dalta hai. Virtualization mein sirf ~20 visible rows ka DOM banta hai; scrollbar ki height ek spacer se fake ki jaati hai.

Design round mein ye "large list" ka standard jawab hai — par akela bolna kaafi nahi, uske tradeoffs bolne padte hain.
lessons.why:
Har DOM node ki memory + layout cost hai. 10k rows = browser 5-10s freeze. Virtualized list mein 20 nodes rehte hain, isliye 10k aur 1M lagbhag same speed pe chalte hain.

Par interview mein ye bolo — virtualization free nahi hai: Ctrl+F kaam nahi karta, SEO mein content dikhta nahi, aur variable-height rows ke liye measurement chahiye. Isliye 200 rows tak mat lagao.

lessons.name: Pagination vs Infinite Scroll
lessons.desc: When each fits, cursor vs offset, back-button support, URL state sync
terms: naya item aane se items ka repeat ya skip ho jaana
lessons.what:
Definition: Bade dataset dikhane ke 3 tarike — numbered pagination, infinite scroll, aur load more button. Aur backend ki taraf do tarike — offset ya cursor.

Design round mein dono decisions alag hain aur dono poochhe jaate hain.
lessons.why:
Offset ka bug jo har interview mein poocha jaata hai: tum page 1 dekh rahe ho, koi naya item top pe add ho gaya. Ab page 2 maango — jo item pehle page 1 ke aakhir mein tha wo neeche khisak ke page 2 ke top pe aa gaya. Tumhe wo dobara dikhega. Delete ho to ek item skip ho jaayega.

Cursor mein ye nahi hota kyunki tum position nahi, pehchan bhejte ho — "is id ke baad wale". Isliye har real-time feed (Twitter, Slack) cursor use karta hai.

lessons.name: Table Design Patterns
lessons.desc: Sorting, multi-column filter, row selection, column resize, pinned columns, sticky header
terms: chaudai mein bhi sirf visible columns render karna
scroll karne pe header upar chipka rehna
logic library deta hai, markup tum likhte ho (TanStack Table)
lessons.what:
Definition: Data table design round ka classic hai kyunki isme sab kuch aata hai — sorting, filtering, pagination, virtualization, column resize, row selection, sticky header, aur responsive.

Sabse zaroori decision: server-side ya client-side? 1000 rows tak client, uske upar server.
lessons.why:
Interview mein log seedha implementation mein ghus jaate hain. Sahi tarika: pehle scale poocho — "kitne rows? 100 ya 10 lakh?" Uske hisaab se poora architecture badal jaata hai:

  • <1000 rows — sab client pe, sort/filter memory mein, koi API nahi
  • >1000 — server-side sorting/filtering/pagination, client sirf dikhata hai
  • >10000 visible — upar se virtualization bhi
where: "design a data table" ek standard question hai
pros: Headless library (TanStack Table) se logic free, styling poora tumhara
Server-side se dataset ka size limit nahi
keepPreviousData se sort/page change pe flicker nahi
cons: Server-side mein har interaction ek network round trip
Column resize + virtualization saath mein kaafi complex
Mobile pe table inherently kharab hai — alag layout chahiye
gotchas: Sabse pehle "kitne rows?" poocho — poora design isi se tay hota hai
Row selection ko id se track karo, index se nahi — sort ke baad index badal jaata hai
Sticky header CSS se karo (position:sticky), JS scroll listener se nahi

lessons.name: Loading / Error / Empty States
lessons.desc: Skeleton screens vs spinners, error boundaries, retry patterns, empty state UX
terms: content ke shape ka grey placeholder
data hai hi nahi wala UI
Cumulative Layout Shift — content aane pe page ka kood-na
lessons.what:
Definition: Har data-driven UI ke chaar states hote hain, teen nahi:

  1. Loading — skeleton (spinner nahi, agar shape pata hai)
  2. Error — kya hua + retry button
  3. Empty — do alag: "kabhi data tha hi nahi" vs "filter se kuch nahi mila"
  4. Success — asli content

Design round mein ye char bolna maturity dikhata hai — junior sirf loading aur success sochta hai.
lessons.why:
Empty state ke do roop hone chahiye kyunki user ki zaroorat alag hai. "Abhi tak koi order nahi" → usse shopping shuru karne ka button chahiye. "Is filter se kuch nahi mila" → usse filter clear karne ka button chahiye. Ek hi "No data" dikhana dono cases mein bekaar hai.

Aur skeleton spinner se behtar hai kyunki wo layout reserve kar leta hai — content aane pe page koodta nahi (CLS = 0).

har widget ke apne char states
pros: Skeleton se CLS zero — page kood-ta nahi
Sahi empty state se user ko agla kadam pata chalta hai
Retry button se transient network error self-heal ho jaata hai
cons: Char states = char UI banana + maintain karna
Skeleton ko content ke saath sync rakhna padta hai
Zyada skeleton se page "busy" lagta hai
gotchas: Do alag empty states banao — "kabhi data nahi tha" aur "filter se nahi mila" bilkul alag hain
Skeleton ki height asli row jaisi rakho warna content aate hi page koodega
Error mein hamesha retry do — bina retry ke error state dead end hai

lessons.name: Optimistic Updates
lessons.desc: Immediate UI feedback, temp IDs, rollback on failure, reconciling with server-pushed data
terms: server ke jawab se pehle hi UI badal dena
server fail hone pe purana state wapas laana
ek hi request do baar bhejo to bhi ek hi asar ho
lessons.what:
Definition: Optimistic update mein tum maan lete ho ki server haan bolega — UI turant update kar dete ho, phir background mein request bhejte ho. Fail ho to purana state wapas.

Teen cheezein zaroori hain: (1) purana state save karo, (2) fail pe rollback, (3) baad mein server se reconcile.
lessons.analogy: Dost se ₹100 maangna. Tum maan lete ho wo de dega aur plan bana lete ho. Mana kar de to plan cancel — par tab tak tumhara time bacha.
lessons.why:
Like button pe 300ms ka wait dikhta hai. Optimistic se app "instant" lagta hai — yahi perceived performance ka sabse bada lever hai.

Par har cheez optimistic nahi honi chahiye. Interview mein ye line bolo: "optimistic tabhi jab fail hone ka chance kam ho aur rollback sasta ho." Like, star, reorder — haan. Payment, delete, checkout — bilkul nahi.
pros: App instant lagta hai — perceived performance ka sabse bada lever
Slow network pe bahut bada fark
Offline-first ki taraf pehla kadam
cons: Rollback logic har mutation mein likhna padta hai
Tez clicking pe race conditions
User ko galat state dikh sakta hai (thodi der ke liye)
gotchas: onMutate mein cancelQueries zaroor karo — warna purana in-flight response tumhara optimistic update mita dega
Irreversible actions (payment, delete) kabhi optimistic mat karo
Rollback ke saath toast dikhao — chup-chaap wapas hona user ko confuse karta hai

lessons.name: Data Normalization
lessons.desc: Flat entity maps vs nested objects, id-to-entity lookup, cache invalidation strategies
terms: nested data ko flat "id → object" maps mein todna
nested tree — jaisa API deta hai
ek entity ka data sirf ek jagah
lessons.what:
Definition: API nested data deta hai — har post ke andar poora author object. Agar ek hi author ke 20 posts hain to wo object 20 baar memory mein hai. Author ka naam badle to 20 jagah badalna padega.

Normalization mein tum data ko flat kar dete ho — { posts: {id: post}, users: {id: user} } — aur post mein sirf authorId rakhte ho.
lessons.analogy: Excel mein har row mein poora address likhna vs ek alag "customers" sheet banake sirf customer-id likhna. Address badle to ek jagah badlo, 500 rows mein nahi.
lessons.why:
Interview mein ye tab aata hai jab entity kai jagah dikhti hai — chat mein user ka naam har message pe, feed mein author har post pe. Bina normalization ke ek update se UI ke aadhe hisse purane reh jaate hain.

Par ye har jagah zaroori nahi. React Query jaise cache ke saath aksar simple invalidate hi kaafi hota hai. Normalization tab lo jab: entity kai jagah dikhe, real-time update aaye, ya offline support chahiye.

Memory kam (duplicate objects nahi)
Real-time patch apply karna trivial ho jaata hai
cons: Read karte waqt jodna padta hai (selectors)
Boilerplate — normalize/denormalize dono likhna
Chhote apps mein bilkul overkill
gotchas: Har jagah mat karo — React Query ke invalidate se aksar kaam chal jaata hai
Order alag rakho (feed: string[]) — object ka key order pe bharosa mat karo
Normalizr jaisi library use kar sakte ho par 30 line ka apna function aksar kaafi hai

lessons.name: Debounce vs Throttle in Search
lessons.desc: When each applies, AbortController for fetch cancellation, cleanup on unmount
terms: rukne ka intezaar karo — aakhri event ke N ms baad chalao
rate limit — har N ms mein zyada se zyada ek baar
window ke aakhir mein chalao ya shuru mein
lessons.what:
Definition: Dono rapid events ko kam karte hain, par soch alag hai:

  • Debounce — "jab tak ruk na jaaye, kuch mat karo". Search input ke liye.
  • Throttle — "chalte raho, par har 200ms mein ek baar". Scroll, resize, mouse-move ke liye.

Search box mein debounce chahiye kyunki har keystroke pe API call bhejna paisa aur rate limit dono barbaad karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Lift ka darwaza. Debounce = koi aa raha ho to ruko, jab 3 second koi na aaye tab band karo. Throttle = har 10 second mein ek baar band hoga, chahe kitne log aayein.
lessons.why:
Design round mein sirf "debounce laga denge" bolna aadha jawab hai. Poora jawab teen hisse ka hai:

  1. Debounce — network calls kam (300ms typical)
  2. Cancel/abort — purani in-flight request ko rok do, warna out-of-order response purane result dikha dega
  3. Cache — same query dobara aayi to network hi mat jao

Sirf debounce se race condition nahi jaati — wo alag problem hai.

lessons.name: Typeahead & Autocomplete Patterns
lessons.desc: Caching strategies, keyboard navigation, match highlighting, no-results state
terms: focus input pe rakhte hue list ka ek item "active" batana
lessons.what:
Definition: Autocomplete design round ka sabse common sawaal hai kyunki isme sab kuch aata hai — debounce, caching, race conditions, keyboard nav, ARIA, virtualization, aur highlighting.

Poora answer 5 layers ka hota hai: input handling → network → cache → keyboard/ARIA → rendering.
lessons.why:
Interviewer dekhta hai ki tum kitni layers yaad rakhte ho. Zyadatar log debounce + fetch bol ke ruk jaate hain. Jo log ye bhi bolte hain wo alag dikhte hain:

  • Keyboard: Arrow up/down, Enter, Escape, Home/End
  • ARIA: role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant — focus input pe hi rehta hai
  • Minimum length (2 chars), aur empty/no-results state
  • Highlight — matched hissa bold, aur user input ko escape karo (XSS)
pros: Cache se same query dobara type karne pe instant
Keyboard nav se power users ko mouse ki zaroorat nahi
Min length se bekaar API calls bach jaate hain
cons: Bahut saari edge cases — blur, click, escape, IME input
Mobile pe keyboard aur dropdown ki jagah ki ladai
Result 1000+ ho to virtualization bhi chahiye
gotchas: onMouseDown pe preventDefault karo — warna input blur ho jaata hai aur click register hi nahi hota
Focus input pe hi rehna chahiye — list item ko focus mat karo, aria-activedescendant use karo
Highlight karte waqt user input escape karo — warna XSS ka rasta khul jaata hai

lessons.name: Form Architecture
lessons.desc: Validation (schema vs field-level), dirty/pristine state, async validation, submit handling
terms: field badla hai kya, user ne chhua hai kya
lessons.what:
Definition: Bade form ka architecture teen decisions hai:

  1. State kahan — controlled (har keystroke pe render) ya uncontrolled (RHF, refs se)
  2. Validation kab — onChange / onBlur / onSubmit, aur schema kahan
  3. Errors kaise — field ke neeche, summary upar, ya dono

Design round ka jawab: uncontrolled + schema validation + onBlur first, onChange after first error.
lessons.why:
30 fields controlled = har keystroke pe 30 components render. RHF uncontrolled rakhta hai, isliye typing pe zero re-render hota hai — sirf error dikhne pe render hota hai.

Validation ka timing UX ka bada hissa hai: onChange se shuru mat karo — user "m" type karega aur "invalid email" dikh jaayega, jo irritating hai. Sahi pattern: pehle onBlur validate karo; ek baar error aa gaya to onChange pe validate karo taaki theek karte hi error hat jaaye.

lessons.name: Keyboard Navigation Design
lessons.desc: Roving tabindex, composite widgets, Home/End/PgUp/PgDn patterns, focus management
terms: Tab dabane pe focus kis order mein jaata hai
modal/menu ke andar focus band rakhna
nav skip karke seedha content pe jaane ka link
lessons.what:
Definition: Keyboard navigation design ka matlab hai — har interaction mouse ke bina bhi ho sake. Char sawaal har widget ke liye:

  1. Focus kahan jaata hai jab widget khule?
  2. Kaunsi keys kya karti hain? (Arrow, Enter, Escape, Tab)
  3. Focus kahan lauth-ta hai band karne pe?
  4. Kya focus fasa hai (modal) ya azaad (dropdown)?
lessons.why:
Ye sirf accessibility nahi — power users bhi keyboard use karte hain. Gmail, Linear, Slack sab keyboard-first hain aur wahi unka competitive advantage hai.

Design round mein jab tum "Escape se band, focus wapas trigger pe" bolte ho, to interviewer ko dikh jaata hai ki tumne asli production component banaya hai.
pros: Power users ko bahut tez workflow
Accessibility compliance apne aap
Interview mein turant senior lagte ho
cons: Har widget ka apna keyboard contract yaad rakhna padta hai
Focus restore ke bahut edge cases (element hat gaya to?)
Testing manual hai — automated test kam pakadte hain
gotchas: Band karne pe focus WAPAS trigger pe bhejo — warna keyboard user page ke top pe pahunch jaata hai
Focusable element ka element hat jaaye to focus body pe chala jaata hai — fallback socho
Radix/React Aria use kar sakte ho — interview mein bolo "production mein Radix, yahan main khud likh ke dikha raha hoon"

lessons.name: Rich Input Patterns
lessons.desc: Multi-select tags, character count, paste handling, drag-to-reorder chips
terms: div ko editable banana — rich text ka base
Input Method Editor — Hindi/Chinese/Japanese typing ka system
cursor ki position khud manage karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Rich inputs — mention (@user), tag input, markdown editor, code editor, masked input (phone, card). Inka common problem ek hi hai: caret (cursor) ki position.

Jab tum programmatically value badalte ho (formatting, masking), browser cursor ko end pe phenk deta hai — user beech mein type kar raha tha to bahut irritating.
lessons.why:
Ye topic isliye poocha jaata hai kyunki ismein tum DOM ke gehre details jaante ho ya nahi ye pata chalta hai — selectionStart, Selection API, aur IME composition events.

Sabse bada trap: IME. Hindi/Chinese type karte waqt onChange har intermediate character pe fire hota hai. Agar tum har change pe API call ya format kar rahe ho to typing hi toot jaati hai. compositionstart/compositionend se pata chalta hai ki user abhi compose kar raha hai.
pros: Sahi caret handling se input professional feel deta hai
IME support se global users ke liye kaam karta hai
Mention/tag se UX bahut natural ho jaata hai
cons: contenteditable ke browser-specific bugs bahut hain
Caret math galat ho to input unusable
Mobile keyboards alag behave karte hain
gotchas: setSelectionRange ko requestAnimationFrame ke andar karo — render se pehle karoge to overwrite ho jaayega
IME (Hindi/Chinese) mein onChange har intermediate char pe firing karta hai — composition events se guard karo
Rich text editor khud mat banao — Lexical ya TipTap lo, aur interview mein yahi bolo

lessons.name: Search State & URL Sync
lessons.desc: Sync filters and query to URL params, back-button support, shareable search URLs
terms: filter/search ko query params mein rakhna
aisa URL jo seedha usi view pe khole
browser history mein ek naya kadam
lessons.what:
Definition: Search query, filters, sort, page, aur open tab — ye sab URL mein hone chahiye, useState mein nahi.

Fayda: shareable link, back button kaam karta hai, refresh pe state bachi rehti hai, aur bookmark ho jaata hai.
lessons.analogy: Kitaab mein bookmark. Page number kitaab mein hi hai — dost ko "page 47 padho" bol sakte ho. Agar page number sirf tumhare dimaag mein hota to share hi nahi kar paate.
lessons.why:
Design round mein ye ek chhota par bahut effective point hai. Jab tum kehte ho "filters URL mein rakhunga taaki user link share kar sake aur back button expected kaam kare" — interviewer ko dikhta hai ki tum user ke perspective se soch rahe ho.

Aur ek zaroori detail: har keystroke pe history entry mat banao. Search typing pe replace: true use karo, warna user ko back dabane pe 30 baar dabana padega.

lessons.name: WebSockets vs SSE vs Polling
lessons.desc: When each fits, connection lifecycle, reconnect strategy, binary vs text frames, fan-out architecture
terms: har N second pe "kuch naya hai?" poochna
Server-Sent Events — server se ek-tarfa stream, HTTP pe
lessons.what:
Definition: Real-time data laane ke teen tarike:

  • Polling — client baar baar poochta hai. Simple, par latency = interval, aur bekaar requests.
  • SSE — server push karta hai, ek direction. HTTP pe chalta hai, auto-reconnect built-in.
  • WebSocket — dono taraf, full duplex. Sabse powerful, sabse zyada infra kaam.
lessons.why:
Interview mein default se WebSocket mat bolo — ye junior signal hai. Sahi jawab requirement se aata hai:

  • Client ko bhejna hai (chat, cursor, collab)? → WebSocket
  • Sirf sunna hai (notifications, live scores, AI token stream)? → SSE — simple, sasta, auto-reconnect
  • Update rare hai (har 30s)? → polling — kuch mat banao

SSE ka bada point: ye normal HTTP hai, isliye proxy/CDN/auth sab bina extra kaam ke chalte hain.

lessons.name: Reconnection & Offline Strategy
lessons.desc: Exponential backoff, navigator.onLine, message queuing while offline, sync on reconnect
terms: har fail pe wait time dugna karna
wait time mein random farak — sab clients ek saath na aayein
server wapas aate hi hazaron clients ek saath connect karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Connection tootegi hi — WiFi badla, tunnel aaya, laptop soya, server deploy hua. Sawaal ye nahi ki tootegi ya nahi, sawaal ye hai ki wapas kaise judegi.

Char cheezein chahiye: (1) exponential backoff + jitter, (2) missed messages ka gap bharna, (3) offline queue, (4) user ko connection status dikhana.
lessons.why:
Thundering herd ye topic ka core hai. Server 30 second ke liye gaya. Wapas aaya. Ab 50,000 clients ek saath reconnect karenge aur server dobara gir jaayega. Jitter isi ka ilaaj hai — har client random time wait kare to load bat jaata hai.

Interview mein "exponential backoff with jitter" bolna — sirf backoff bolne se kaafi behtar hai.

lessons.name: Optimistic UI for Mutations
lessons.desc: Temp IDs, rollback pattern, reconciling optimistic state with server-pushed updates
terms: wo message jo bheja gaya par confirm nahi hua
server ka jawab aane pe temp ko asli se replace karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Chat mein message bhejte hi wo screen pe dikhna chahiye — server ke confirm ka intezaar nahi. Iske liye chahiye:

  1. Temp id (uuid) se message turant list mein daalo, status sending
  2. Server ka jawab aane pe temp id ko asli id se replace karo
  3. Fail ho to status failed + retry button — message hatao mat
lessons.why:
Ye normal optimistic update se alag hai kyunki yahan identity ka problem hai — client ne id banayi, server ne apni banayi, aur beech mein WebSocket se wahi message dobara aa sakta hai (echo). Bina temp-id mapping ke duplicate dikhega.

Aur fail hone pe message ko hatana nahi chahiye — user ne type kiya hai, wo mehnat hai. Failed state + retry sahi UX hai.
pros: App instant lagta hai chahe network slow ho
Failed message bacha rehta hai — user ki mehnat nahi jaati
tempId se echo aur duplicate handle ho jaate hain
cons: Message list mein teen alag states manage karni padti hain
Ordering: pending message aur server message ka order mismatch
Offline mein queue persist karni padti hai (localStorage/IndexedDB)
gotchas: tempId server ko bhejo aur wapas maango — yahi echo/duplicate ka saaf ilaaj hai
Failed message kabhi delete mat karo — status badlo aur retry do
Ordering ke liye server timestamp use karo, client ka nahi (clocks alag hote hain)

lessons.name: Presence & Typing Indicators
lessons.desc: Throttle broadcasts, cleanup on disconnect, showing multiple user cursors
terms: har N second pe "main zinda hoon" bhejna
temporary data jo DB mein save nahi hota
lessons.what:
Definition: Presence (online/offline) aur typing indicators ephemeral data hain — DB mein save nahi hote, sirf memory/Redis mein short TTL ke saath rehte hain.

Do standard patterns: presence heartbeat + TTL se, typing throttled event + auto-expire se.
lessons.why:
Naive typing indicator har keystroke pe event bhejta hai — 60 messages per minute per user. 50 log ke room mein ye 3000 messages/min hai, sirf "typing" ke liye. Sahi tarika: throttle (3 second mein ek "typing" event) aur receiver side pe auto-expire (5 second baad khud hata do).

Auto-expire isliye zaroori hai kyunki "stopped typing" event kho sakta hai (tab band, network gaya) — tab indicator hamesha ke liye atka reh jaayega.

Bade room (1000+) mein har user ki presence mat bhejo — count bhejo ya sirf active few

lessons.name: Notification Architecture
lessons.desc: Push vs pull, unread badge count, grouping similar notifications, mark-as-read strategies
terms: ek event ko kai users tak pahunchana
kai similar notifications ko ek mein jodna
lessons.what:
Definition: Notification system design round mein aata hai kyunki isme frontend + backend dono ka soch chahiye. Frontend side pe char hisse hain:

  1. Delivery — SSE/WebSocket (live) + REST (history)
  2. State — unread count, read/unread, per-notification actions
  3. Grouping — "5 logon ne like kiya" (25 alag rows nahi)
  4. Cross-tab sync — ek tab mein padha to doosre tab mein bhi
lessons.why:
Cross-tab sync wo detail hai jo bahut kam log bolte hain. User ke 3 tabs khule hain. Ek mein notification padha — baaki do mein badge abhi bhi "3" dikha raha hai. BroadcastChannel se ye ek line mein theek ho jaata hai.

Aur grouping zaroori hai kyunki bina uske popular post 200 notifications bana deta hai aur user notification band kar deta hai.
pros: SSE se live delivery sasti aur simple
Grouping se notification fatigue kam
BroadcastChannel se cross-tab sync lagbhag muft
cons: Read state ko server + kai tabs mein sync rakhna
Grouping ke rules product-specific hote hain
Browser notification permission ka UX nazuk hai
gotchas: Cross-tab sync zaroor mention karo — BroadcastChannel bahut kam log jaante hain
Notification permission page load pe mat maango — user ke kisi action ke baad maango
Unread count server se lo — client pe list se ginoge to paginated list mein galat hoga

lessons.name: Conflict Resolution Basics
lessons.desc: Last-write-wins, operational transforms, CRDTs — concept level, when each applies
terms: jo baad mein aaya wahi jeeta — simple par data kho sakta hai
Operational Transform — Google Docs ka purana tareeka
Conflict-free Replicated Data Type — apne aap merge ho jaane wala data
lessons.what:
Definition: Do log ek hi cheez ek saath badlein to kya ho? Teen strategies:

  • LWW — timestamp se jo baad ka wo jeeta. Simple. Doosre ka kaam chup-chaap gum.
  • OT — har operation ko doosre ke hisaab se transform karo. Powerful, par central server chahiye aur likhna bahut mushkil.
  • CRDT — data structure aisa banao ki merge hamesha same natija de. Server ki zaroorat nahi, par memory zyada.
lessons.analogy: Do log ek hi Google Doc mein likh rahe hain. LWW = jiska save baad mein hua uska version bacha, doosre ka gaya. CRDT = dono ke words apne apne jagah pe rehte hain, kuch nahi khota.
lessons.why:
Interview mein CRDT khud implement karne ki koi ummeed nahi hai. Ummeed ye hai ki tum:

  1. Conflict ko pehchano — "do log ek saath edit karein to?"
  2. Product ke hisaab se sahi strategy chuno — form field pe LWW theek hai, text editor pe nahi
  3. Library ka naam jaano — Yjs (CRDT), Automerge

Aur ek practical fallback: field-level locking — "Riya is field ko edit kar rahi hai" — bahut saare business apps ke liye ye kaafi hai aur banane mein 1 din lagta hai.

lessons.name: SPA Routing Architecture
lessons.desc: Code splitting at routes, nested routes, auth guards, scroll restoration, 404 handling
terms: har page ka apna JS chunk
route ka data render se pehle laane wala function
ek cheez ke baad doosri — parallel nahi, isliye slow
lessons.what:
Definition: SPA routing architecture ke char decisions:

  1. Code splitting — har route apna chunk (lazy + Suspense)
  2. Data loading — loader se render se pehle, ya component ke andar
  3. Nested layouts — sidebar/nav navigate karne pe re-render na ho
  4. Prefetch — hover/viewport pe agla route pehle hi laao
lessons.why:
Interview ka core point waterfall hai. Purana pattern: route match → chunk download → component render → useEffect → data fetch. Ye teen sequential steps hain — 300ms + 200ms + 400ms.

Loader-based routing mein router ko route match karte hi pata hai kaunsa data chahiye, isliye chunk aur data parallel chalte hain. Aur nested routes mein saare matching loaders ek saath chalte hain, ek ke baad ek nahi.

lessons.name: State Management Architecture
lessons.desc: Local vs server state, React Query vs Redux vs Zustand, when each fits, avoiding over-engineering
terms: server ka data jiski tumhare paas copy hai
sirf browser ka state — modal, draft, theme
filter, tab, page — address bar mein
lessons.what:
Definition: "State management" ek cheez nahi, char alag cheezein hain — aur har ek ka apna tool hai:

  1. Server state → React Query / SWR / RTK Query
  2. URL state → searchParams
  3. Global client state → Zustand / Jotai / Context
  4. Local state → useState / useReducer

Design round mein ye char bolna hi asli jawab hai — "Redux use karunga" nahi.
lessons.why:
90% "state management ka dard" server state ko client state ki tarah treat karne se aata hai. Server data ko cache, refetch, dedup, stale detection chahiye — Redux ye kuch nahi deta, isliye log ye sab haath se likhte hain aur store 5000 line ka ho jaata hai.

Server state alag kar do, URL state alag kar do — jo global client state bachta hai wo aksar itna kam hota hai ki Zustand ka 30-line store kaafi hai.

lessons.name: Authentication & Authorization
lessons.desc: JWT in memory, HTTP-only cookie refresh token, silent renew, RBAC, BroadcastChannel logout
terms: chhoti umar ka token jo har request ke saath jaata hai
lambi umar ka token jo naya access token deta hai
aisi cookie jise JavaScript padh hi nahi sakta
lessons.what:
Definition: Frontend auth ke teen hisse:

  1. Token kahan rakhein — httpOnly cookie (safe) vs localStorage (XSS mein chori ho jaata hai)
  2. Refresh kaise — 401 pe ek hi refresh chale, saare pending requests uska intezaar karein
  3. Authorization — kya dikhana hai (UI) aur kya karne dena hai (server)
lessons.why:
Sabse important line jo interview mein bolni hai: frontend authorization sirf UX hai, security nahi. Button chhupane se koi API safe nahi hoti — user DevTools se request bhej sakta hai. Asli check hamesha server pe.

Aur token storage: localStorage mein token XSS se chori ho jaata hai. httpOnly cookie JS se padhi hi nahi jaa sakti — par CSRF ke liye SameSite=Strict ya CSRF token chahiye. Ye tradeoff bolna zaroori hai.
pros: httpOnly cookie XSS se token bacha leti hai
Single-flight refresh se refresh storm nahi hota
Cross-tab logout se security consistent
cons: Cookie ke saath CSRF protection alag se chahiye
Refresh logic ke bahut edge cases (refresh khud 401 de to?)
Permissions client pe rakhna = payload bada
gotchas: "Frontend authorization sirf UX hai, security server pe hai" — ye line zaroor bolo
localStorage mein token XSS mein chori ho jaata hai — httpOnly cookie prefer karo aur tradeoff batao
Refresh ko single-flight karo warna 10 parallel 401 pe 10 refresh calls chalengi

lessons.name: Error Boundary Strategy
lessons.desc: Granularity decisions, fallback UI quality, error reporting (Sentry), retry mechanisms
terms: ek error se kitna hissa toota
ek hissa toote to baaki chalta rahe
minified stack trace ko asli code se jodne wali file
lessons.what:
Definition: Error boundary strategy ka matlab hai — kahan kahan boundaries lagani hain taaki ek widget ka crash poora app na le doobe.

Teen level: root (aakhri safety net), route (ek page toota, nav chalta rahe), widget (ek chart toota, dashboard chalta rahe).
lessons.analogy: Jahaaz ke watertight compartments. Ek compartment mein paani bhar jaaye to poora jahaaz nahi doobta — bas wo hissa seal ho jaata hai.
lessons.why:
React 16 se ek uncaught error poora app unmount kar deta hai — safed screen. Sirf root pe boundary lagane se safed screen ki jagah "Kuch gadbad hui" aa jaata hai, par user ka kaam phir bhi gaya.

Design round mein blast radius ka sochna seniority dikhata hai: "third-party chart widget ka apna boundary hoga, taaki uska crash mere dashboard ko na le doobe."

lessons.name: Performance Budget & Monitoring
lessons.desc: Bundle size limits, LCP/INP/CLS targets, CI enforcement, real user monitoring (RUM)
terms: ek limit — "bundle 200KB se upar nahi jaayega"
Real User Monitoring — asli users ka data, lab test nahi
75th percentile — 75% users isse behtar experience paate hain
lessons.what:
Definition: Performance budget = numbers jo CI mein enforce hote hain. Bina budget ke performance dheere dheere kharab hoti jaati hai aur kisi ko pata nahi chalta.

Do tarah ka measurement: lab (Lighthouse, CI mein) aur field/RUM (asli users, web-vitals library se). Dono chahiye — lab regression pakadta hai, RUM sach batata hai.
lessons.why:
Interview mein numbers bolna bahut fark laata hai. "Fast banayenge" vs "LCP p75 under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1, aur initial JS 200KB gzipped" — doosra jawab senior ka hai.

Aur p75 pe naapna zaroori hai, average pe nahi — average ko kuch tez devices chhupa dete hain. Google ke Core Web Vitals bhi p75 pe hain.

lessons.name: Internationalization (i18n)
lessons.desc: Locale detection, RTL support, dynamic string chunk loading, pluralization, date/number formatting
terms: localization — asli translation aur regional formatting
plural/gender handle karne wala message syntax
lessons.what:
Definition: i18n sirf strings translate karna nahi hai. Paanch hisse hain:

  1. Strings — keys + translation files, lazy load per locale
  2. Plurals & gender — ICU format (har bhasha ke rules alag)
  3. Formatting — date, number, currency (Intl API)
  4. RTL — Arabic/Hebrew ke liye layout mirror
  5. Locale detection — URL, cookie, ya Accept-Language
lessons.why:
Sabse aam galti: string concatenation. "You have " + n + " items" translate hi nahi ho sakta kyunki har bhasha ka word order alag hai, aur plural rules alag hain — Russian mein 4 plural forms hain, Arabic mein 6. ICU format isliye hai.

Doosri galti: saari bhashaon ki translations ek bundle mein. 20 languages × 50KB = 1MB, jisme se user sirf 50KB use karta hai. Locale-wise lazy load karo.
pros: Intl API browser mein built-in — koi library nahi
ICU se plural/gender har bhasha mein sahi
Logical CSS properties se RTL lagbhag free
cons: Translation workflow (TMS, translators) ka apna process
Text expansion — German 30% lamba hota hai, layout tootta hai
Testing har locale mein karna padta hai
gotchas: String concatenation kabhi mat karo — ICU message format use karo
CSS mein margin-left ki jagah margin-inline-start likho — RTL apne aap kaam karega
Layout ko text expansion ke liye tayyar rakho — German/Finnish mein text 30-40% lamba hota hai
